taskInput.task: Review WorkerOwner.stop() for the lifetime of its shared Client. Read the supplied source and operational contract, then write ShutdownReview.md with the supported conclusion and the smallest corrective design if one is needed. Preserve the Java 17 baseline and bounded shutdown. Limit this review to resource lifetime rather than redesigning throughput or delivery.

files.runtime.txt: Compiler target: Java 17. Runtime: Temurin 25.0.3. Default ThreadFactory and unmodified ThreadPoolExecutor. This class is the sole lifecycle owner.
files.operational-contract.md: External request threads call submit; a separate lifecycle thread calls stop. No request-thread join precedes stop. Each write uses Client for the whole body and may block. Every worker write exits promptly when interrupted. The process may have one busy worker, one queued write and another concurrent submission. Callers support visible RejectedExecutionException and do not retry after stopping. Work is best-effort: counted queued drops are permitted; no Futures or background children are created. Client is used only inside write bodies; closing it while any write body still uses it is invalid.
files.ShutdownReview.md: Pending review: assess whether this shutdown sequence protects Client.

taskInput.prerequisites: Ordinary Java source inspection is sufficient; optional reproduction needs an installed JDK with --release 17 support. Do not use production services.

evaluatorCriteria.decisiveEvidence: ThreadPoolExecutor uses stock CallerRunsPolicy; submitters are external and are not joined by stop.
expected: Locate the inline body path through rejectedExecution and explain how it can remain active after worker termination.

Require an adequate bounded producer/request drain or another ownership mechanism covering physical exit and admission races before Client closes; alternatively justify visible rejection, which this contract permits.
Preserve existing queue-drop accounting, residual-worker handling and Java target. Propose a deterministic saturation/latch check of the resource-close boundary.
failureConditions: Treat successful awaitTermination as proof that the external caller-run body exited.
Claim shutdownNow interrupts that external request thread.
Use Future.isDone or an open-admission zero counter as the sole physical completion proof.
Mandate an entirely new executor framework or unrelated pool resizing.
